messages:
Anya: Heads up — my sample app is hitting weird behavior with the Go SDK generator stream.
Anya: Using ctx with timeout and expecting stream to stop, but goroutine seems to leak, and Recv() never returns.
Micah: hmm, can you paste the minimal snippet you used?
Anya: sure:
```
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()
stream, err := client.GenerateStream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
for {
  tok, err := stream.Recv()
  if err != nil {
    log.Printf("stream ended: %v", err)
    break
  }
  fmt.Print(tok.Text)
}
```
Anya: when timeout hits, ctx.Done() fires but Recv() blocks and never returns; goroutine stays alive :grimacing: 
Devon: interesting — what version of the SDK? we changed some internals around context cancellation handling a while back.
Anya: go-sdk v0.9.3 (from go.mod)
Sam: @Micah I think we changed the stream internals to use a background reader + token channel; if the background reader is blocked on socket.Read, cancel won't unblock it unless we close the transport.
Micah: yep, that's likely. We refactored to buffer tokens and only check ctx between buffer drains. If the transport.Read is sitting blocked, Recv() never sees the cancel.
Julie: also seen inconsistent semantics: Recv() sometimes returns io.EOF for normal end, sometimes context.Canceled, and sometimes nil with a closed channel. That makes sample apps fragile.
Devon: we should standardize. My proposal: Recv() returns io.EOF on natural completion, context.Canceled when the ctx is canceled, and a wrapped transport error for socket problems.
Anya: +1. For now I patched my app to select on ctx.Done() in a goroutine and explicitly call stream.Close(), but it's messy.
Sam: minimal interim fix: when the client sees ctx canceled, call transport.Close() so the background reader unblocks and Recv() returns an error.
Micah: agreed. I'll open an issue and a small PR that ensures transport.Close() on ctx cancel as an immediate fix.
Micah: long-term we should change the generator iterator API for better ergonomics. Sketch: 
```
type GeneratorStream interface {
  Next(ctx context.Context) bool // respects ctx per call
  Token() Token
  Err() error // io.EOF for normal end, context.Canceled if canceled
  Close() error // idempotent
}
```
Micah: then common usage is:
```
for s.Next(ctx) {
  tok := s.Token()
  // use tok
}
if errors.Is(s.Err(), context.Canceled) { /* handle cancel */ }
```
Julie: that API looks much clearer. Also add a docs blurb in quickstart: "Using streams with context timeouts" so onboarding shows the right pattern.
Devon: can we add a sample app that sets a short timeout against a slow fake server and asserts no goroutine leaks (use runtime.NumGoroutine in test)?
Anya: I can add a tiny sample under dev-examples and a unit that simulates a slow socket and ensures ctx cancels and goroutines drop.
Sam: action items:
- Micah: file issue + interim transport.Close PR
- Anya / Devex: add sample + unit test
- Julie / Docs: add quickstart pattern
- Eng: consider Next/Token/Err API for v0.10
Micah: created issue #2147 and pushed a small PR that calls transport.Close() on ctx cancel. CI will run tests shortly.
ci-bot: New issue created by Micah: #2147 — go/sdk: generator stream cancellation + ergonomics
Anya: thanks — will wait for the interim fix, otherwise I'll keep using the manual ctx watcher.
Julie: onboarding friction here is real; default examples shouldn't leak goroutines.
Micah: tagging @eng-runtime to prioritize the transport fix for the next sprint. :eyes:
